label: which is …
note: Comments on everything just said, not only the last word.
example: He played all night, which is wild.

label: which means …
note: Draws a consequence from the previous point.
example: The server is down, which means no ranked tonight.

label: which is why …
note: Gives the reason for what comes next.
example: I hate that map, which is why I always dodge it.

label: the thing is …
note: Introduces the real issue or the catch.
example: The thing is, nobody read the patch notes.

label: the problem is …
note: Points to what is going wrong.
example: The problem is the timer resets.

label: the point is …
example: The point is we still won.

label: the funny thing is …
example: The funny thing is, he wasn't even trying.

label: the way (that) …
note: Talks about how something is done.
example: The way he rotates is so clean.

label: the fact that …
note: Turns a whole statement into a thing you can react to.
example: The fact that it worked is insane.

label: the reason (why) …
example: The reason why I left is the lag.

label: what's the point …
example: What's the point of saving it?

label: that's what I'm saying
re: \b(?:that's what i'm saying|what i'm saying is|that's all i'm saying)\b
note: Agrees strongly, or restates your point.
example: That's what I'm saying, it's broken.

label: it's not like …
note: Rejects an idea someone might have.
example: It's not like I wanted to lose.

label: if that makes sense
example: You hold it, then release, if that makes sense.

label: as long as …
note: Only if this condition is true.
example: We're fine as long as we keep the high ground.

label: as soon as …
example: As soon as I spawned, I died.

label: even though …
example: Even though we lost, that was fun.

label: even if …
example: Even if he flanks, we hold.

label: unless …
example: Don't push unless I call it.

label: in case …
note: To be ready if something happens.
example: Grab a shield in case they rush.

label: so that …
example: Stand there so that they can't see you.

label: whereas …
example: He plays safe, whereas I just run in.

label: rather than …
example: Rather than waiting, let's go now.

label: instead of …
example: Use the pistol instead of the rifle.

label: as if …
note: In a way that suggests (often not true).
example: He acts as if he's never played before.

label: no matter what …
example: No matter what I do, it crashes.

label: whether or not …
example: Whether or not it's fair, it's the rule.

label: to the point where …
note: So much that something else happens.
example: I laughed to the point where I cried.

label: let alone …
example: I can't aim, let alone snipe.

label: not to mention …
note: Adds one more, often bigger, point.
example: It's slow, not to mention expensive.

label: on top of that …
example: On top of that, my mic died.

label: on the other hand …
example: On the other hand, it looks great.

label: speaking of …
example: Speaking of food, I'm starving.

label: in terms of …
example: In terms of speed, nothing beats it.

label: as far as I know
note: From what I know (I might be wrong).
example: As far as I know, it's still in beta.

label: that being said …
re: \b(?:that being said|having said that|with that being said)\b
note: Turns to a different side after a point.
example: That being said, I'd still buy it.

label: that's why …
note: Gives the result of a reason.
example: That's why I never trust him.

label: if anything …
note: Actually, it's the opposite (or more so).
example: If anything, it got worse.

label: after all
note: Reminds of a fact, or 'in the end'.
example: It worked after all.

label: in the first place
note: At the very start (often with blame).
example: Why did you go there in the first place?

label: the more …, the more …
example: The more I play, the worse I get.

label: at the end of the day
example: At the end of the day, it's just a game.

label: at this point
note: Now, after all that has happened.
example: At this point, just restart.

label: at some point
example: We'll fix it at some point.

label: for some reason
example: For some reason, it only lags here.

label: all of a sudden
example: All of a sudden, three guys showed up.

label: for the most part
example: For the most part, chat is nice.

label: in a way
example: In a way, losing helped.

label: at least
note: The minimum, or one good thing.
example: At least we got the skin.

label: first of all
note: Starts a list of points (often an argument).
example: First of all, that wasn't me.

label: by the way
example: By the way, thanks for the sub.

label: I mean …
example: I mean, it's not that bad.

label: you know what …
note: Announces a decision or a new thought.
example: You know what, let's do it.

label: to be fair …
note: Admits a point for the other side.
example: To be fair, he warned us.

label: to be honest …
example: To be honest, I'm tired.

label: not gonna lie
example: Not gonna lie, that was clean.

label: let's be real
note: Asks everyone to admit the truth.
example: Let's be real, nobody reads the rules.

label: kind of / sort of
example: It's kind of weird.

label: pretty much
example: We pretty much won.

label: or something / or whatever
re: \b(?:or something(?: like that)?|or whatever|and stuff(?: like that)?|and all that)\b
note: Keeps a list or detail vague.
example: Get some snacks or something.

label: I feel like …
example: I feel like this build is better.

label: I guess …
note: Not fully sure, or reluctantly agreeing.
example: I guess we try again.

label: I bet …
example: I bet he's camping.

label: I swear …
example: I swear I hit him.

label: low-key / high-key
note: Low-key: a little, quietly. High-key: openly, a lot.
example: This song low-key slaps.

label: for real
example: For real, that was close.

label: I was like …
re: \b(?:i was|he was|she was|they were|we were|i'm|he's|she's|they're|everyone was|chat was|chat's) like\b
note: Introduces what someone said or thought, in stories.
example: And I was like, no way.

label: literally
example: I literally just got here.

label: used to …
note: True in the past, not now.
example: I used to main support.

label: get used to …
example: You get used to the recoil.

label: end up …
note: Finally be or do something, often unplanned.
example: We ended up staying till 3.

label: be about to …
example: I'm about to lose it.

label: was gonna …
note: A plan in the past that didn't happen or got interrupted.
example: I was gonna say that.

label: supposed to …
note: Expected or planned (but maybe not happening).
example: You're supposed to wait.

label: might as well …
note: There's no better option, so do it.
example: Might as well try.

label: would rather …
example: I'd rather lose than cheat.

label: had better …
example: You'd better run.

label: make sure …
example: Make sure you save first.

label: figure (it) out
example: We figured it out.

label: come up with …
note: Think of an idea or plan.
example: He came up with a new strat.

label: get rid of …
example: Get rid of that sword.

label: run out of …
example: I ran out of ammo.

label: look forward to …
example: I'm looking forward to the update.

label: it turns out …
example: Turns out he was right.

label: it depends (on) …
example: It depends on the team.

label: can't help (but) …
example: I can't help but laugh.

label: can't stand …
example: I can't stand that sound.

label: can't wait …
example: Can't wait for the finals.

label: gotta …
example: I gotta go.

label: worth it / worth …
note: Good enough to justify the cost.
example: Totally worth it.

label: hang out
example: Let's hang out after stream.

label: mess up
example: I messed up the timing.

label: give up
example: Don't give up yet.

label: I was wondering …
example: I was wondering if you could help.

label: it is what it is
example: We lost. It is what it is.

label: no way
example: No way he hit that.

label: fair enough
example: Fair enough, your call.

label: my bad
example: My bad, wrong button.

label: no offense
note: Softens something that might sound rude.
example: No offense, but that was bad.

label: you never know
example: Buy a ticket, you never know.

label: no wonder
example: No wonder it's lagging.

label: it's been a while
example: It's been a while since I played this.

label: so much for …
example: So much for an easy win.

label: how come …
example: How come you're always late?

label: what if …
example: What if we go left?

label: guess what
example: Guess what, I got it.

label: I'm down
example: I'm down to play later.

label: that makes sense
example: Oh, that makes sense.

label: here we go
example: Here we go again.

label: what do you mean …
example: What do you mean it's gone?
